## Tailor the tool to your course/module {#tailor-the-tool}

You can give your students a tailored link: a version of this tool that only offers the categories of AI use your course/module or assignment allows. Tick the allowed categories, untick any tasks within them that are not allowed, and optionally add your course/module title. If a use of AI your assignment allows isn't covered, you can add your own categories and tasks. Students who open the link see your course/module title (if you added one), and Step 1 is filled in and locked to your selection. In Step 2 they can only describe the tasks you allowed.

Share the link on your Learning Management System (LMS) course site or in your syllabus. Your assignment brief remains the authority.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
data = FileAttachment("taxonomy.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function el(tag, props = {}, children = []) {
  const node = document.createElement(tag);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(props)) {
    if (v === undefined || v === null) continue;
    if (k.startsWith("on") && typeof v === "function") {
      node.addEventListener(k.slice(2), v);
    } else if (k === "checked" || k === "value" || k === "disabled") {
      node[k] = v;
    } else if (k === "class") {
      node.className = v;
    } else {
      node.setAttribute(k, v);
    }
  }
  for (const child of [].concat(children)) {
    if (child === null || child === undefined) continue;
    node.append(child instanceof Node ? child : document.createTextNode(child));
  }
  return node;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Builds the module link that index.qmd reads (see its `preset` cell), e.g.
// ?module=Comparative+Politics&allow=lit-write&not=write.trans&c1=Survey+design&c1=Wording+survey+questions&v=1
// All state lives inside this cell, so typing doesn't re-run anything else.
linkBuilder = {
  // category id -> Set of allowed task ids. Absent means not allowed.
  const allowed = new Map();
  const allItems = cat => new Set(cat.items.map(i => i.id));
  // Categories the lecturer writes themselves: { name, tasks: [text] }.
  const custom = [];
  const MAX_CUSTOM = 5;
  const MAX_TASKS = 10;
  const namedCustom = () => custom.filter(c => c.name.trim());
  // The tool's own page, so the link also works on a local preview.
  const base = new URL("./", window.location.href).href;

  const moduleInput = el("input", { type: "text", id: "gaidet-link-module", class: "gaidet-link-input", autocomplete: "off", placeholder: "e.g., Comparative Politics" });
  const assignmentInput = el("input", { type: "text", id: "gaidet-link-assignment", class: "gaidet-link-input", autocomplete: "off", placeholder: "e.g., Essay 1" });
  const catList = el("div", { class: "gaidet-category-gate-list" }, []);
  const customList = el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-custom-list" }, []);
  const urlBox = el("code", { class: "gaidet-link-url" }, []);
  const status = el("span", { class: "gaidet-link-status", role: "status" }, []);
  const problemNote = el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-instructions" }, []);
  // Opens in its own window (reused for later checks) next to the builder,
  // rather than a tab; a plain new tab if the browser blocks the window.
  const tryLink = el("a", {
    target: "_blank",
    rel: "noopener",
    onclick: (e) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      const checkWindow = window.open(tryLink.href, "gaidet-link-check", "popup,width=1200,height=900");
      if (checkWindow) {
        checkWindow.opener = null;
        checkWindow.focus();
      } else {
        window.open(tryLink.href, "_blank", "noopener");
      }
    }
  }, "Open the link in a new window to check it");
  const copyButton = el("button", { type: "button", class: "gaidet-btn-primary gaidet-link-copy" }, "Copy link");

  function buildUrl() {
    const params = new URLSearchParams();
    const moduleTitle = moduleInput.value.trim();
    if (moduleTitle) params.set("module", moduleTitle);
    const assignment = assignmentInput.value.trim();
    if (assignment) params.set("assignment", assignment);
    const cats = data.categories.filter(cat => allowed.has(cat.id));
    if (cats.length) params.set("allow", cats.map(cat => cat.key).join("-"));
    // Excluded tasks only, as category.task, since there are usually few.
    const excluded = cats.flatMap(cat =>
      cat.items.filter(i => !allowed.get(cat.id).has(i.id)).map(i => `${cat.key}.${i.key}`));
    if (excluded.length) params.set("not", excluded.join("-"));
    // Own categories as c1=Category&c1=Task&c1=Task (see index.qmd).
    namedCustom().forEach((c, i) => {
      params.append(`c${i + 1}`, c.name.trim());
      c.tasks.map(t => t.trim()).filter(Boolean).forEach(t => params.append(`c${i + 1}`, t));
    });
    // The taxonomy version, so categories and tasks added later can be
    // flagged as new instead of read as not allowed (see index.qmd).
    params.set("v", Math.max(...data.categories.flatMap(cat => [cat, ...cat.items]).map(e => e.added ?? 1)));
    return `${base}?${params}`;
  }

  function renderLink() {
    const url = buildUrl();
    const problem = allowed.size === 0 && namedCustom().length === 0 ? "Select at least one category to create a link." : "";
    urlBox.textContent = url;
    problemNote.textContent = problem;
    problemNote.hidden = !problem;
    copyButton.disabled = !!problem;
    tryLink.hidden = !!problem;
    // Jumps straight to the generator, where the course settings show.
    tryLink.href = `${url}#generate-declaration`;
    status.textContent = "";
  }

  function renderCategories() {
    const focusedId = document.activeElement?.id;
    catList.replaceChildren(...data.categories.map(cat => {
      const isAllowed = allowed.has(cat.id);
      const option = el("label", {
        class: "gaidet-category-gate-option" + (isAllowed ? " gaidet-category-gate-option-checked" : "")
      }, [
        el("input", {
          type: "checkbox",
          class: "gaidet-checkbox-input",
          role: "switch",
          id: `gaidet-link-cat-${cat.key}`,
          checked: isAllowed,
          onchange: (e) => {
            if (e.target.checked) allowed.set(cat.id, allItems(cat)); else allowed.delete(cat.id);
            render();
          }
        }),
        el("span", { class: "gaidet-switch", "aria-hidden": "true" }, [el("span", { class: "gaidet-switch-thumb" }, [])]),
        el("span", {}, cat.label),
        isAllowed && cat.items.length > 1
          ? el("span", { class: "gaidet-link-count" }, `${allowed.get(cat.id).size} of ${cat.items.length} tasks`)
          : null
      ]);
      if (!isAllowed || cat.items.length < 2) return option;

      const tasks = el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-tasks", role: "group", "aria-label": `Allowed tasks in ${cat.label}` }, cat.items.map(item => {
        const mark = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "svg");
        mark.setAttribute("viewBox", "0 0 24 24");
        mark.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
        mark.setAttribute("class", "gaidet-checkbox-mark");
        mark.innerHTML = '<path d="M5 13l4 4L19 7" pathLength="1"/>';
        return el("label", { class: "gaidet-category-gate-option gaidet-link-task" }, [
          el("input", {
            type: "checkbox",
            class: "gaidet-checkbox-input",
            id: `gaidet-link-task-${cat.key}-${item.key}`,
            checked: allowed.get(cat.id).has(item.id),
            onchange: (e) => {
              const set = allowed.get(cat.id);
              if (e.target.checked) set.add(item.id); else set.delete(item.id);
              // Unticking the last task turns the whole category off.
              if (set.size === 0) allowed.delete(cat.id);
              render();
            }
          }),
          el("span", { class: "gaidet-checkbox-box" }, [mark]),
          el("span", {}, item.label)
        ]);
      }));
      return el("div", {}, [option, tasks]);
    }));
    if (focusedId) document.getElementById(focusedId)?.focus();
  }

  // Typing only refreshes the link; adding or removing a field rebuilds
  // this list, then moves focus to the field just added (if any).
  function renderCustom(focusId) {
    const textInput = (id, value, placeholder, label, onInput) => el("input", {
      type: "text", id, class: "gaidet-link-custom-input", value, placeholder, maxlength: "100",
      autocomplete: "off", "aria-label": label,
      oninput: (e) => { onInput(e.target.value); renderLink(); }
    });
    const removeButton = (label, onclick) =>
      el("button", { type: "button", class: "gaidet-link-remove", "aria-label": label, onclick }, "×");

    customList.replaceChildren(...custom.map((c, ci) => el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-custom" }, [
      el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-custom-row" }, [
        textInput(`gaidet-link-custom-${ci}`, c.name, "Category name, e.g., Survey design", `Name of your category ${ci + 1}`, v => { c.name = v; }),
        removeButton(`Remove category ${ci + 1}`, () => { custom.splice(ci, 1); renderCustom(); renderLink(); })
      ]),
      el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-custom-tasks" }, [
        ...c.tasks.map((t, ti) => el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-custom-row" }, [
          textInput(`gaidet-link-custom-${ci}-${ti}`, t, "Task, e.g., Wording survey questions", `Task ${ti + 1} in category ${ci + 1}`, v => { c.tasks[ti] = v; }),
          removeButton(`Remove task ${ti + 1}`, () => { c.tasks.splice(ti, 1); renderCustom(); renderLink(); })
        ])),
        c.tasks.length < MAX_TASKS ? el("button", {
          type: "button", class: "gaidet-link-quick",
          onclick: () => { c.tasks.push(""); renderCustom(`gaidet-link-custom-${ci}-${c.tasks.length - 1}`); }
        }, "+ Add a task") : null,
        el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-instructions" }, "Optional. Without tasks, students tick the category itself.")
      ])
    ])));
    if (custom.length < MAX_CUSTOM) {
      customList.append(el("button", {
        type: "button", class: "gaidet-link-add",
        onclick: () => { custom.push({ name: "", tasks: [] }); renderCustom(`gaidet-link-custom-${custom.length - 1}`); }
      }, "+ Add your own category"));
    }
    if (focusId) document.getElementById(focusId)?.focus();
  }

  function render() {
    renderCategories();
    renderLink();
  }

  moduleInput.addEventListener("input", renderLink);
  assignmentInput.addEventListener("input", renderLink);

  let statusTimer;
  copyButton.addEventListener("click", async () => {
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(buildUrl());
      status.textContent = "Link copied";
    } catch {
      status.textContent = "Copying was blocked. Select the link above and copy it.";
    }
    clearTimeout(statusTimer);
    statusTimer = setTimeout(() => { status.textContent = ""; }, 3000);
  });

  const selectAll = el("button", { type: "button", class: "gaidet-link-quick", onclick: () => {
    data.categories.forEach(cat => allowed.set(cat.id, allItems(cat)));
    render();
  } }, "Select all");
  const clearAll = el("button", { type: "button", class: "gaidet-link-quick", onclick: () => {
    allowed.clear();
    render();
  } }, "Clear");

  render();
  renderCustom();

  return el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-builder" }, [
    el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-field" }, [
      el("label", { class: "gaidet-tool-label", for: "gaidet-link-module" }, ["Course/module title ", el("span", { class: "gaidet-link-optional" }, "(optional)")]),
      moduleInput,
      el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-instructions" }, "We recommend a specific title, such as the course/module code and year, so students can tell it apart from their other courses/modules. Nothing you enter here is stored: the title only becomes part of the link, which is created in your browser.")
    ]),
    el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-field" }, [
      el("label", { class: "gaidet-tool-label", for: "gaidet-link-assignment" }, ["Assignment title ", el("span", { class: "gaidet-link-optional" }, "(optional)")]),
      assignmentInput,
      el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-instructions" }, "Add this if the rules differ between assignments in the same course/module.")
    ]),
    el("div", { class: "gaidet-category-gate" }, [
      el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-label gaidet-step-label" }, "Which categories of AI use does the assignment allow?"),
      el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-instructions" }, "All tasks in a category are allowed when you tick it. Untick any task you want to exclude."),
      catList,
      el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-quick-row" }, [selectAll, clearAll]),
      el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-custom-section" }, [
        el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-label" }, "Missing a category?"),
        el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-instructions" }, "Add up to five of your own, each with its own tasks if you like. Students see them as allowed, marked “Added by your lecturer”."),
        customList
      ])
    ]),
    el("div", { class: "gaidet-link-result" }, [
      el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-label gaidet-step-label" }, "Your tailored link"),
      el("p", { class: "gaidet-tool-instructions" }, "Students who open this link see the tool with the settings you chose above."),
      urlBox,
      el("div", { class: "gaidet-output-actions gaidet-link-actions" }, [copyButton, tryLink, status]),
      problemNote
    ])
  ]);
}
```

## Frequently asked questions

::: {.gaidet-faq-accordion}
### Where do these categories come from? {.gaidet-faq}

The categories in Step 1 of the tool are drawn from task categories used in student surveys and existing AI disclosure guidelines. They form a checklist of common use cases, not a recommendation that students use AI for all, or indeed any, of them. Whether AI is appropriate for a given category still depends entirely on your assignment brief and your own instructions.

Step 1 is the crucial filtering step for students: it should reflect only what your assignment or course/module actually permits, not everything AI happens to be capable of. Students who are unsure whether a category applies are told to leave it unticked and ask you rather than guess.

### How can I phrase permitted AI use in my assignment brief? {.gaidet-faq}

Some lecturers find it useful to name the same categories in their assignment brief as the ones in Step 1, rather than describing permitted and prohibited AI use in separate wording. Students can then tick exactly what has been permitted without having to interpret how a general policy applies to their situation.

One way this can look in an assignment brief:

::: {.gaidet-quote}
For this assignment, you may use AI for *Conceptualisation* and *Initial literature screening*, for instance to brainstorm ideas or locate relevant sources. AI must **not** be used for *Data management*, *Coding and automation*, *Writing and editing*, or *Audiovisual and interactive components*, as these should be your own unassisted work. Anything else can be recorded under *Additional tasks*. Please use the AI Disclosure Generator to record your AI use and attach the generated declaration to your assignment submission: [https://disclose-ai.app](https://disclose-ai.app).
:::

If you [tailored the tool to your course/module](#tailor-the-tool), share your tailored link in place of the general address so that Step 1 is already filled in for your students.

### What if my course/module has not settled on an AI policy yet? {.gaidet-faq}

A student who ticks "no guidance" in Step 1 is told to treat that as AI not being permitted, rather than as permission by default, until you or the course/module coordinator confirms otherwise. Settling on even a brief policy, using the wording above, removes that ambiguity for your students.

### Where can I find related tools, literature, and advice? {#related-literature-and-advice .gaidet-faq}

A number of similar tools exist to support transparent AI-use disclosure, including the [AID Framework](https://aidframework.org), the [GAIDeT Declaration Generator](https://panbibliotekar.github.io/gaidet-declaration/), and [sIfA](https://github.com/mareikeschomerus-ctrl/sIfA) (Statement of Intellectual Fellowship and Accountability), a browser-based tool from Busara that maps AI contributions onto the 14 CRediT contributor roles and is aimed more at researchers documenting a publication than at student coursework. All aim at the same goal: helping students and researchers disclose their AI use clearly and consistently. Use whichever fits your context best.

The optional "AIAS level" field in the tool uses the [AI Assessment Scale](https://aiassessmentscale.com), a complementary framework instructors use to specify how much AI use is permitted on a given assessment; this tool only lets you record that level, it doesn't set or enforce it.

This tool's approach is comparable to the [American Journal of Political Science's AI Policy](https://ajps.org/ajps-ai-policy/), which asks authors to describe how AI was used rather than reproduce full transcripts. If you're an instructor who wants students to submit the entire output of their AI conversations, not just a summary and the prompts used, ask for that separately.

Further reading on AI-use disclosure:

- Suchikova, Yana, Tsybuliak, Natalia, Teixeira da Silva, Jaime A., & Nazarovets, Serhii (2026). “GAIDeT (Generative AI Delegation Taxonomy): A Taxonomy for Humans to Delegate Tasks to Generative Artificial Intelligence in Scientific Research and Publishing“. *Accountability in Research*, *33*(3). [10.1080/08989621.2025.2544331](https://doi.org/10.1080/08989621.2025.2544331)
- Weaver, Kari D. (2024). “The Artificial Intelligence Disclosure (AID) Framework: An Introduction“. *College & Research Libraries News*, *85*(10), 407–411. [arxiv.org/abs/2408.01904](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.01904)
- Perkins, Mike, Furze, Leon, Roe, Jasper, & MacVaugh, Jason (2024). “The AI Assessment Scale (AIAS)“. [aiassessmentscale.com](https://aiassessmentscale.com)
- American Journal of Political Science (2026). “AJPS AI Policy“. Updated 11 August 2026. [ajps.org/ajps-ai-policy](https://ajps.org/ajps-ai-policy/)
- Saleh, Engy, & Schomerus, Mareike (2026). “The sIfA Tool for a Statement of Intellectual Fellowship and Accountability: An Invitation to Reflect on How Humans and AI Interact in Producing Knowledge“. *Busara*. [10.62372/IUPB2137](https://doi.org/10.62372/IUPB2137)
- Schomerus, Mareike. *sIfA Tool (Tool to create a Statement of Intellectual Fellowship and Accountability)*. Version 1.4. 2026. *Busara*. [10.5281/zenodo.20285993](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20285993)
:::

```{=html}
<script>
// Turns each question in the lecturers FAQ above into a collapsible
// <details> item: the "?" heading becomes the summary and everything up to
// the next question becomes the answer. Quarto may or may not wrap each
// heading in its own <section>, so both layouts are handled.
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const root = document.querySelector(".gaidet-faq-accordion");
  if (!root) return;

  // Answers slide open with a slight overshoot and slide shut, instead of
  // jumping. Pattern after beUI's Bouncy Accordion (https://beui.dev, MIT
  // licence). Skipped when the visitor has asked for reduced motion, which
  // leaves the plain <details> toggle.
  const reduceMotion = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)");
  const toggleAnimated = (details, answer) => {
    const closing = details.classList.contains("is-closing");
    const startHeight = details.open ? answer.offsetHeight : 0;
    answer.getAnimations().forEach(a => a.cancel());
    answer.style.overflow = "hidden";
    const done = () => { answer.style.overflow = ""; };
    if (!details.open || closing) {
      details.classList.remove("is-closing");
      details.open = true;
      answer.animate(
        [{ height: `${startHeight}px`, opacity: closing ? 1 : 0 }, { height: `${answer.scrollHeight}px`, opacity: 1 }],
        { duration: 380, easing: "cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.3, 0.64, 1)" }
      ).onfinish = done;
    } else {
      details.classList.add("is-closing");
      answer.animate(
        [{ height: `${startHeight}px`, opacity: 1 }, { height: "0px", opacity: 0 }],
        { duration: 220, easing: "ease-in" }
      ).onfinish = () => {
        details.classList.remove("is-closing");
        details.open = false;
        done();
      };
    }
  };
  for (const h of [...root.querySelectorAll("h3.gaidet-faq")]) {
    const section = h.parentElement.matches("section.level3") ? h.parentElement : null;
    const body = [];
    if (section) {
      body.push(...[...section.children].filter(n => n !== h));
    } else {
      for (let n = h.nextElementSibling; n && !n.matches("h3.gaidet-faq"); n = n.nextElementSibling) body.push(n);
    }
    const details = document.createElement("details");
    details.className = "gaidet-faq-item";
    // Put the new item where the question was, before moving anything.
    (section ?? h).before(details);
    const summary = document.createElement("summary");
    summary.className = "gaidet-faq-summary";
    summary.append(h);
    const answer = document.createElement("div");
    answer.className = "gaidet-faq-answer";
    answer.append(...body);
    details.append(summary, answer);
    // Quarto puts a question's id (e.g. #related-literature-and-advice) on
    // its section, so keep it on the new item for links to still find it.
    if (section?.id) details.id = section.id;
    section?.remove();
    summary.addEventListener("click", e => {
      if (reduceMotion.matches) return;
      e.preventDefault();
      toggleAnimated(details, answer);
    });
  }

  // Links to a question (e.g. #related-literature-and-advice from "About
  // this tool") open its answer rather than landing on a closed item.
  const openFromHash = () => {
    const target = location.hash ? root.querySelector(location.hash) : null;
    const details = target?.closest("details.gaidet-faq-item");
    if (details) {
      details.open = true;
      target.scrollIntoView();
    }
  };
  openFromHash();
  window.addEventListener("hashchange", openFromHash);
});
</script>
```
